name: SeaCloudAI Sandbox

plans.name: Public rate not established
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

caveats: Published SDK supplies SeaArt-hosted control/build/runtime endpoint. No public dollar tariff established; SDK distribution alone is not a proof of ungated signup.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshot APIs are not exposed yet because the underlying platform does not support them.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Same sentence in the Go and Node SDK READMEs. Only pause/resume and custom template builds.

harness_api.note: Official 'claude' / 'codex' templates only have 'the CLIs preinstalled' (agent_harnesses); SDKs and CLI expose lifecycle, files, commands, PTY, git, code interpreter, templates only. No API to prompt/stream/resume an in-sandbox agent. The seacloud CLI's 'llm run' calls hosted models, not an in-sandbox harness.

egress_allowlist.quote: AllowInternetAccess=false enables egress isolation. AllowOut and DenyOut accept IPv4 CIDR ranges or single IPv4 addresses
egress_allowlist.note: Per-sandbox SandboxNetworkPolicy at create or via PUT /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/network (seacloud CLI 'sandbox network update --allow-internet-access=false --allow-out 1.1.1.1 --deny-out 10.0.0.0/8'). IPv4/CIDR only, no domains. Enforcement point not documented. The Python SDK 0.3.2 still rejects 'network' / 'allow_internet_access' on create ('is not supported'); the Go SDK v0.3.4 and CLI expose it.

ingress_rules.quote:
Network policy can control public inbound traffic, internet egress, and explicit
egress allow/deny CIDR lists.
ingress_rules.note: allowPublicTraffic flag on the network policy; get_host(port) gives a proxy URL derived from envdUrl, with a sandbox-scoped traffic_access_token (E2B-style). No IP allowlist documented.

volume_attach.quote:
Volumes are durable storage resources that can be mounted during sandbox create
with --volume-mount name:/path.
volume_attach.note: Named volumes (POST /api/v1/volumes) mounted at create via volumeMounts name:path. Template volumeMounts also support NFS host paths, block volumes (storageClass/storageSizeGB), PVCs and object-bucket mounts with readOnly flag. Sizes/prices unpublished.

nested_virt.quote: Run code, agent workflows, and lightweight services in isolated cloud sandboxes from Python.
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; a code/agent-execution sandbox gateway with no mention of /dev/kvm or nested virtualization.

desktop.quote: The SDK gives you a simple E2B-style workflow for sandbox lifecycle, files, commands, PTY, code execution, service proxying, and reusable template builds.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no VNC/RDP/stream desktop surface documented anywhere in the SDKs or CLI.

browser.quote: Official templates for fast starts: use base for files, commands, git, and PTY; use code-interpreter for multi-language code execution; use agent templates such as claude or codex
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no managed/real browser template or API documented.

computer_use.quote: Run code, agent workflows, and lightweight services in isolated cloud sandboxes from Python.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; there is no desktop, so no screenshot+click driving API exists.

anti_bot.quote: Run code, agent workflows, and lightweight services in isolated cloud sandboxes from Python.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; a headless code/agent sandbox with no browser product, so no stealth/fingerprinting feature exists.

captcha_solving.quote: Run code, agent workflows, and lightweight services in isolated cloud sandboxes from Python.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no browser/CAPTCHA feature documented.

ssh.note: Interactive access is via the sandbox gateway's own command/PTY runtime protocol and access-token proxy (get_host/traffic_access_token), not a real SSH server/port. No SSH mentioned anywhere in the SDKs or CLI.

snapshot.quote: Snapshot APIs are not exposed yet because the underlying platform does not support them.
snapshot.note: Same statement repeated in Go/Node SDK READMEs. Only pause/resume (not full snapshot/restore) and template builds are supported.

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshot APIs are not exposed yet because the underlying platform does not support them.
snapshot_auto.note: No snapshot capability exists at all, so there is no automatic state save/restore on stop/sleep.

fork.quote: Main Entrypoints - Sandbox.create(...), Sandbox.connect(...), Sandbox.list(...): create and manage sandboxes.
fork.note: No clone/fork-a-sandbox API documented; only create-from-template, connect, list, pause/resume, delete.

fork_running.quote: Main Entrypoints - Sandbox.create(...), Sandbox.connect(...), Sandbox.list(...): create and manage sandboxes.
fork_running.note: derived: no fork feature exists at all, so cloning a running machine is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Snapshot APIs are not exposed yet because the underlying platform does not support them.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork capability exists, so memory-preserving clones are not possible.

wake_on_request.note: The 'auto-resume' create flag and pause command note ('Pause a sandbox so it can be resumed later when auto-resume routing is enabled') describe the gateway router auto-resuming a paused sandbox when a request arrives.

volume_shared.quote:
Volumes are durable storage resources that can be mounted during sandbox create
with --volume-mount name:/path.
volume_shared.note: Named volumes are created independently of any one sandbox (seacloud sandbox volume create) and mounted by name into any sandbox via --volume-mount, implying the same volume can be mounted by multiple sandboxes; not explicitly confirmed for concurrent mounts.

auto_stop_idle.quote: sandboxCreateCmd.Flags().BoolVar(&sandboxCreateOpts.autoPause, "auto-pause", false, "Pause instead of kill on timeout")
auto_stop_idle.note: auto-pause pauses (rather than deletes) a sandbox when its lifecycle timeout elapses; this is timeout-based rather than activity-based idle detection, so evidence is indirect.

live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are fixed fields on the sandbox detail set at creation/template build; no API to change them on a running sandbox is documented (only SetTimeout for the lifecycle timeout).

own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; 'seacloud llm run'/'seacloud run' call hosted third-party generative models (LLM/image/video), not a first-party browser/computer-use/research task agent that drives the sandbox itself.

mcp_server.quote: intentionally not exposed yet: MCP server helpers and devcontainer helpers
mcp_server.note: Same line appears in the Python and Go SDK READMEs' template helper lists.

public_ipv4.quote: Use sandbox.get_host(port) when you start an HTTP service and want a public proxy URL.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is exposed only via a proxy URL derived from envdUrl/traffic_access_token (E2B-style), not a routable public IPv4 address assigned to the machine.

egress_http_rules.quote: AllowOut and DenyOut accept IPv4 CIDR ranges or single IPv4 addresses; single IPs are normalized by the control plane to /32.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is IP/CIDR-level only (no domain or HTTP method/path level rules documented).

secret_proxy.quote: sandbox.files.write(...) result = sandbox.commands.run("sh", args=[...]) ... export SEACLOUD_API_KEY=...
secret_proxy.note: No first-party credential-injection HTTP proxy is documented; env vars (envVars on create) are the only documented way to pass secrets into a sandbox.

gpu.quote: Run code, agent workflows, and lightweight services in isolated cloud sandboxes from Python.
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; a code/agent sandbox product with no GPU machine type mentioned in SDKs, CLI, or template build options (only cpu-count/memory-mb).

windows.quote: Prebuilt binaries are published on the Releases page for: macOS amd64, macOS arm64, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, Windows amd64
windows.note: Windows/macOS binaries are the CLI tool for the operator's own machine; the sandbox guest OS itself is Linux-only per official templates (base, code-interpreter, claude, codex all run Linux commands like uname -a, apt_install).

macos.quote: Prebuilt binaries are published on the Releases page for: macOS amd64, macOS arm64, Linux amd64, Linux arm64, Windows amd64
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; sandbox guest machines are Linux containers/VMs (apt_install, Dockerfile-style base images), no macOS guest option documented.

self_host.quote: The SeaCloudAI production gateway is currently hosted under the seaart.ai domain.
self_host.note: SDKs/CLI target a hosted SeaCloudAI gateway (with a dev override URL for SeaCloudAI's own environments); no self-hosted/on-prem deployment of the sandbox platform itself is offered to customers.

byoc.quote: The SeaCloudAI production gateway is currently hosted under the seaart.ai domain.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; only SeaCloudAI's own hosted gateway is documented, no bring-your-own-cloud deployment option.

open_source.note: Only the client SDKs (Python/Go/Node) and CLI are MIT-licensed open source; the sandbox execution platform/gateway itself is closed-source and hosted by SeaCloudAI, so the core product is not open source.

sso.quote: seacloud auth login seacloud auth status seacloud auth set-key <api-key>
sso.note: Documented auth is a browser-based device-flow login and API keys only; no SAML/OIDC SSO option is documented anywhere.

egress_ip_type.quote: The SDK validates the archive size before upload and sends the required GCS content-length-range header.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: build-context uploads go through a GCS (Google Cloud Storage) content-length-range header and the template builder offers from_gcp_registry/from_aws_registry, indicating standard hyperscaler-cloud infrastructure. No residential, mobile, or dedicated/static egress IP feature is documented anywhere in the SDKs or CLI; outbound traffic is only controllable via AllowOut/DenyOut CIDR lists, not IP type.

persistent_disk.quote: Snapshot APIs are not exposed yet because the underlying platform does not support them.
persistent_disk.note: derived: there is no documented 'stop' lifecycle distinct from pause/kill/delete. pause()/resume() keep an existing sandbox suspended (billing-relevant, not disk persistence across a stop/start cycle), and disk/filesystem snapshotting is explicitly stated as unsupported by the platform, so files are not documented to survive a full stop/start.

guest_firewall.note: derived: default examples operate as root (writes under /root/workspace, uname -a via plain sh -lc with no sudo), consistent with full guest OS/root access. Per card convention, root-capable guests are assumed to allow nftables/iptables to function inside, though this is not separately documented.

static_egress_ip.quote: Egress allowlist IPv4/CIDR, repeatable or comma-separated
static_egress_ip.note: The only outbound-IP-related feature documented is a per-sandbox allow/deny CIDR list controlling which destinations a sandbox may reach (egress_allowlist); no SDK/CLI field or doc offers a fixed/dedicated outbound IP address for a sandbox.

eu_data_residency.quote: SEACLOUD_BASE_URL: required full gateway API root
eu_data_residency.note: derived: there is no --region flag or region parameter anywhere in the CLI, SDKs, or API types; sandbox creation only targets a single configured gateway base URL (production example: sandbox-gateway.cloud.seaart.ai). No region/data-residency selection is documented, so EU residency cannot be offered as a controllable feature.
